issue_context.title: Syntax highlighting highlights `$` syntax on node names starting with a number, despite not being valid identifiers
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot Engine v4.0.beta10.official.d0398f62f

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Even though the syntax highlighting is correct, the following errors are raised, unless quotes are used.

`Expected node path as string or identifier after "$".`
`Invalid numeric notation.`
`Expected statement, found "Literal" instead.`

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a node named "2D" to the scene
2. In a script, use `$2D`
3. The errors above are shown, even though the highlighting works fine

### Minimal reproduction project

[node-starts-with-number.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10332763/node-starts-with-number.zip)
comments: Didn't think nodes starting with numbers were permitted?

Can you reproduce this on 3.5.1?

This is expected, as valid identifiers must not start with a number. The syntax highlighting should be fixed as to not highlight these as valid node paths though.

> Can you reproduce this on 3.5.1?
> 
> This is expected, as valid identifiers must not start with a number. The syntax highlighting should be fixed as to not highlight these as valid node paths though.

It's the same on 3.5.1.

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
  print($2D.name) # error
  print($"2D".name) # 2D
  print(get_node("2D").name) # 2D
  print(get_node(@"2D").name) # 2D
  
  var a = Node2D.new()
  a.name = "123456"
  add_child(a)
  print(a.name) # 123456
```

Using "2D" and "123456" as node paths seems to work correctly (both on 3.x and 4), so if we want to disallow them to start with a number we should probably throw an error.
Hmm... okay. I'm a bit confused why we only allow identifiers tbh

review_comments:
I'm not familiar with that code, but isn't it possible to rely on the same method that guarantees a valid identifier for nodes to do the completion, instead of reimplementing it?
We have `String::is_valid_identifier()` which I think handles this, though not 100% it's consistent with what is done here, or what `Node::validate_node_name()` does.

Valid node names are not always valid identifiers. Only valid identifiers are allowed in GDScript without using quotations, however. I think this is to make parsing easier - since many of the allowed symbols have special meanings in GDScript.)

Either way, it'd be more inconvenient to do that, since this part of the highlighter works character by character to figure out if it should flip bools.
Makes sense. You might be interested in checking if `core/string/char_utils.h` has useful functions to reuse in this parser, but this PR can be merged as is in the meantime.
